problem: Learned ObjectNav policies (end-to-end and modular) had been evaluated almost only in simulation. Prior sim-to-real studies covered PointNav and locomotion, not semantic navigation, so nobody knew whether sim results, sim design choices or sim error modes predict real-robot performance for navigating to objects.
motivation: Hundreds of semantic-navigation methods and many sim benchmarks exist, but what matters is how a method performs on a robot. Without real-world evaluation the field risks sim-only research that does not generalize. The authors observe that sim RGB is far from photo-realistic, while abstractions such as top-down semantic maps look nearly the same in sim and reality. This suggests modular, abstraction-based policies should transfer better than pixel-to-action policies.
key_idea: Run a large-scale real-world ObjectNav study: classical (frontier), modular-learning (SemExp) and end-to-end (Habitat-Web) policies, all trained or tuned in Habitat, are deployed on a Hello Robot Stretch in 6 unseen homes (60 episodes), plus one home replicated in sim, to measure sim-to-real transfer and compare error modes.
insight: Modularity and abstraction drive transfer. The semantic map (5 cm cells, category channels) is nearly invariant between sim and real, while the RGB space has a large gap. A segmentation model trained in sim falls from 0.45 to 0.10 mAP@0.5 in the real world, and a real-trained one falls from 0.50 to 0.35 when applied to sim. The end-to-end ablation (Table 1) shows sim performance can be inversely related to real performance. Policy 1 (sim camera, sim-trained segmentation, IL+RL) is best in sim (0.77 SR) but worst in the real home (0.00 SR, SRCC 0.20). Policy 4 (robot camera, real-trained Mask R-CNN, IL only) is worst in sim (0.48) but best in real (0.30, SRCC 0.60), so both sim-trained segmentation and RL fine-tuning overfit to sim. Sim and real error modes barely overlap. Modular real failures are mostly depth-sensor errors (5/6: depth noise closing doors, mirror/TV reflections), which sim with perfect depth never shows. Sim failures come from reconstruction artifacts: segmentation errors (10.1%) and navmesh errors (5.5%) out of 18.6% failures. This is why modular SR rises from sim to real, and why SRCC stays only 0.70 even for modular.
method: Study design: three representative ObjectNav policies (classical, modular learning, end-to-end), 6 real homes never seen in sim or reality, 60 episodes over 6 categories (chair, couch, potted plant, toilet, tv, bed). Start positions are chosen to match the Habitat Challenge 2022 geodesic-distance distribution. About 45 robot-hours; success = STOP within 1 m, 200-step and 20-collision budgets.

Sim-to-real I/O matching: Stretch RealSense D435i RGB-D (640x480, 42° HFOV) with spatial/temporal depth filters, depth thresholded at 4 m. Pose comes from LiDAR-based Hector SLAM; LiDAR is used only for localization and collision detection, never mapping. The fairo library runs the same code in Habitat and on the robot. Discrete actions: FORWARD 25 cm, TURN 30°, STOP.

Modular learning (SemExp): Mask R-CNN (ResNet-50, MS-COCO) segmentation is projected with depth and pose into a 3D voxel map, then summed over height into a K=C+4 channel 2D semantic map (5 cm cells). A CNN + FFNN exploration policy, trained with RL on Gibson layouts (reward = distance reduced to nearest goal), outputs a long-term goal every 25 steps. A Fast Marching Method planner replans every step, and navigation switches to the goal once it appears in the map.

Classical baseline: same semantic mapping and FMM planner, but SemExp's learned exploration is replaced by frontier exploration (closest frontier in geodesic distance, goal-agnostic). This gives depth-first-search-like behaviour.

End-to-end (Habitat-Web): a frozen segmentation model feeds a PointNav-pretrained ResNet-50 depth encoder and from-scratch ResNet-18 RGB/semantic encoders. These, plus pose, goal embedding, goal-pixel fraction and previous action, go into a GRU that predicts actions. It is trained by IL on 80k human demos (~20M actions, 3 days on 128 V100s), optionally followed by RL fine-tuning for 150M steps. It is retrained with robot camera parameters, and variants are ablated over camera parameters, segmentation training domain (sim RedNet vs real Mask R-CNN) and IL vs IL+RL.

Controlled sim replica + SRCC: one home is scanned with a Matterport Pro2 and its 10 episodes are replicated in Habitat. This splits the benchmark-to-real gap into benchmark vs replica and replica vs real. Sim-vs-Real Correlation Coefficient = Pearson correlation of binary episode outcomes.

Error analysis: on the sim benchmark, programmatic ablations (GT segmentation, 2000-step budget) plus manual labelling of remaining failures (navmesh vs goal-annotation errors). Real episodes are categorized as depth-noise, reflection, segmentation or exploration failures.

setting.backbone: Modular: Mask R-CNN ResNet-50 (MS-COCO, frozen) + CNN/FFNN semantic-exploration policy (SemExp, RL-trained) + FMM planner. End-to-end: Habitat-Web GRU policy with ResNet-50 depth / ResNet-18 RGB+semantic encoders (retrained). Classical: same mapping + frontier exploration (no learned policy).
setting.training_data: SemExp exploration policy: RL on Gibson home layouts (policy from Chaplot et al. 2020). End-to-end: IL on 80,000 Habitat-Web human ObjectNav demonstrations (~20M actions) in Habitat/HM3D, retrained with robot camera parameters, optionally plus RL fine-tuning for 150M steps. Segmentation: Mask R-CNN pretrained on MS-COCO (real images); the sim-segmentation variant uses RedNet pretrained on SUN RGB-D and fine-tuned on Habitat images.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (RealSense D435i, 640x480, 42° HFOV) + pose (LiDAR Hector SLAM on robot) + goal category
setting.action_space: discrete FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 30° / STOP (FMM planner outputs low-level actions for modular/classical)
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3D Semantics, Habitat Challenge 2022 ObjectNav; plus a Matterport-scanned replica of one real home)
setting.privileged: none (pose from onboard LiDAR Hector SLAM; LiDAR also used for collision detection but not for mapping)

numbers_note: Some results are printed only in the Fig. 3 bar chart or only per home/category. Sim-benchmark SPL for all methods, and real-world SPL for classical and end-to-end, appear only in the Fig. 3 bar chart (not transcribed). Per-home and per-category SR/SPL are in Table S2. On the 10-episode single home and its sim replica (Table 1), sim replica SR / real SR / SRCC are: Modular 0.80/0.90/0.70, Classical 0.80/0.90/0.70, End-to-end 4 0.50/0.30/0.60, End-to-end 1 0.80/0.00/0.20. The 77% sim vs 23% real contrast for end-to-end in Fig. 3 compares different variants: policy 1 in sim vs policy 4 in real (policy 4's sim SR is 0.48). Modular sim SR 81.4% includes 157 goal-annotation-error episodes counted as success; raw is 733/1093. On all 2000 val episodes, including multi-floor, modular succeeded in 1078/2000. Success uses a 1 m threshold, not the Habitat Challenge's standard criterion.
results: Modular learning (SemExp) transfers best: 90% SR and 0.64 SPL on 60 real-world episodes, up from 81% in sim. Classical frontier exploration reaches 80% real (78% sim). End-to-end Habitat-Web collapses to 23% real SR, against 77% for the best-in-sim variant. In the controlled single-home study, sim performance of end-to-end variants was inversely related to real performance (policy 1: 0.77 sim / 0.00 real; policy 4: 0.48 sim / 0.30 real). SRCC is at most 0.70, because modular failures in reality are mostly depth-sensor errors, whereas sim failures stem from segmentation (10.1%) and navmesh (5.5%) reconstruction artifacts.
limitations: Small real-world sample: 60 episodes, 6 homes, 10 per home; only one representative method per class, 6 closed-set goal categories, single-floor episodes.

No abstraction-based end-to-end variant was tested (e.g., a policy on semantic frames), and no robot-specific depth or actuation noise models were simulated. The Habitat depth noise model hurt real performance.

Sim and real protocols differ: 500 vs 200 steps, and a 1 m success radius. The modular sim SR counts manually re-labelled annotation errors as success, so absolute sim numbers are not directly comparable with standard HM3D ObjectNav leaderboards.
